summary: SvgDocument.createExporter returns a namespace-scoped exporter retaining one last successfully exported immutable definition set and its validated definition map, element/semantic identities and direct-node/path-segment counts. Structural definition equality permits reuse; changed definitions receive full validation. Document headers, instances, references, cross-definition identity collisions, combined limits and instance-dependent expanded-symbol limits remain live checks. Failed exports cannot certify definitions, and SvgDocumentBrowserHost resets its owned exporter on disposal. Stateless exportSvg keeps the existing contract; full export, parsing and DOM reconciliation still occur on accepted Replace calls. Four public-contract tests cover ordered result/byte parity, invalid transitions, numeric/reference/identity boundaries and aggregate node/segment/expansion limits; six separately compiled unsafe-cache mutants were killed and restored source/assembly were checked. The local three-pair A/A plus three-pair A/B public-circle Chromium153 software comparison passed the unchanged 10% relative gate across 20 cells but no cell improved beyond tolerance. At250 with10% sparse motion the paired-median ratio was0.998733 and candidate p95 was68.9–80.6ms. B5 remains8.33ms at250 licensed shared glyphs on Home; this different geometry/software profile cannot evaluate it. Additional local browser correctness required explicit Chromium153 and private fallback fonts after identical baseline/candidate ambient-font failures; normal pinned-browser/coherent CI remains separate. These are local candidate source and measurement observations under Delivery1496, not proof of merge, Home/GPU, publication, installed adoption or parent4645 completion. The owning SVG plan and native issue retain the full remaining promise.
title: Definition-validation reuse retains independent instance and aggregate checks
